data.name: Amitanshu
data.gender_notes: Amitanshu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Amitanshu is a name derived from the Sanskrit words 'amita' meaning 'infinite' or 'boundless' and 'anshu' meaning 'ray of light' or 'prosperity'. The name Amitanshu carries the meaning “Boundless Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amitanshu usually hope their child will grow to embody boundless prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizing infinite prosperity, this name reflects spiritual abundance and divine grace.
data.etymology: Amitanshu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Boundless Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amitanshu total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Amitanshu" carries a deep cultural significance in Hinduism. It is believed that Hindu deities, especially Lord Vishnu and Lord Shiva, have infinite (amita) rays of light or shakti bestowed upon them. The name Amitanshu can be seen as a nod to the divine and infinite power that these deities possess.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name "Amitanshu" signifies the idea of infinite light or knowledge. It can serve as a reminder to individuals that the knowledge and truths they seek in life exist in an infinite and boundless form, just as the name suggests. Additionally, the name may inspire the bearer to illuminate others with their own ray of knowledge and prosperity, acting as a beacon of light in their community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amitanshu: Unending, boundless truth or perfection. Radiating supreme consciousness and wisdom.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads, yet a beautiful name.

historical_references.reference: Amitanatha, the 12th Tirthankara of Jainism, born around 11th century BCE in Magadha, India. The name 'Amitanatha' is derived from Sanskrit words 'amita' meaning infinite and 'anatha' meaning lord. This name symbolizes the infinite and selfless nature of the Tirthankara.
Amitabha, a Buddhist deity, symbolizing infinite light and infinite life. Believed to be the Buddha of the Western Paradise, Sukhavati. The name 'Amitabha' in Sanskrit means 'infinite light'.
